# @vllnt/convex-slugs

> Convex component for unique slugs, handles and usernames per scope, with rename redirects, a TypeScript client and React hooks.

Install `@vllnt/convex-slugs` (unreleased builds from `main` use the `canary`
dist-tag). Peer dependency `convex@^1.45.0`; optional `react@>=18` for
`@vllnt/convex-slugs/react`. Mount it with `app.use(config)` from
`@vllnt/convex-slugs/convex.config` and call it through
`new Slugs(components.slugs, options?)` from host mutations and queries.
Methods: `reserve`, `release`, `rename`, `resolve`, `redirectFor`,
`slugForResource`. Uniqueness is per `(scope, slug)` and rides the Convex
mutation transaction. Slugs are normalized with NFC, `trim()` and (by default)
`toLowerCase()`. `rename` records an old -> new redirect and collapses chains.
`reserve` and `rename` return `{ ok: false, reason }` (`SLUG_INVALID`,
`SLUG_RESERVED`, `SLUG_TAKEN`, `SLUG_NOT_FOUND`) instead of throwing. Invalid
input throws `ConvexError` with `data.code` `INVALID_OPTIONS` or
`INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Defaults: scope `"global"`, `minLength` 1, `maxLength` 256.
`reserve` and `rename` cap writes at 1024 UTF-16 code units (`string.length`):
a longer slug returns `SLUG_INVALID`, a longer `scope` or `resourceRef` throws
`INVALID_ARGUMENT`; `release` and the queries are not capped.
The host owns auth and the meaning of the opaque `resourceRef`. React hooks
`useSlugAvailable` and `useResolve` take the host's own public query.

## When to use

- Use it when each public name (article slug, `@handle`, username, workspace
  slug) must be unique inside a scope, even under concurrent claims.
- Use it when renaming must keep old URLs working through a redirect.
- Use it when you need lookups both ways: slug to resource and resource to slug.
- Do not use it when the key must stay secret (share links, magic links,
  invites): a slug is meant to be public (it appears in URLs). Use
  [`@vllnt/convex-tokens`](https://oss.vllnt.com/packages/convex-tokens).

## For coding agents

The docs are bundled in the package at `node_modules/@vllnt/convex-slugs/docs/`
and match the installed version. Read them, and the shipped `src/`, before
writing code. The links below to `./` paths are files inside the installed package.
